messages:
Anna: quick heads-up — on the private VPC small-gpu pool (low-ram nodes) we started seeing a p95 token latency climb ~20% after the kernel-selector tweak last night. likely related to batching behavior + KV cache churn. anyone on call to triage?
Raj: looking now. which pool exactly? t4-small?
Anna: yes t4-small-1 / tenant: acme-internal. reproduction fairly consistent with steady-state traffic.
Maria: if KV cache eviction is firing more often that could blow up cold KV miss latencies. did the kernel selector change alter sequence-length routing?
Anna: good Q — kernel selector moved some small-seq requests onto the newer fused-kernel path; profiler shows more micro-batches forming with more prefix mismatches.
Kevin: grabbing a profile. share trace: `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" https://private.console/trace/trace-1859004321`
perf-bot: [alert] private:t4-small-1 p95 latency +19% over 30m window (triggered by kernel-selector rollout) :warning:
Raj: hypothesis: batching heuristic is forming larger batches based on request count threshold instead of token-budget, so mixed-length sequences cause KV cache pressure + kernel fallback penalties.
Maria: propose quick experiment: override batching knobs on the pool with lower max_batch_size and strict token_budget_target, plus increase queue_timeout_ms to avoid eagerly packing long seqs. e.g.
```
# override for private pool (one-off)
batching.max_batch_size: 8
batching.token_budget_target: 1024
batching.queue_timeout_ms: 12
kernel.selection.allow_fallback:true
kv.eviction_threshold_pct: 65
```
Raj: also try batch_formation.mode: token_aware (instead of count_aware) — token_aware will group by token budget, reduces mixed-length noise.
Anna: can we patch these live for that tenant only? don't want global change.
Kevin: yes, we have per-pool overrides. I can push a canary to acme-internal pool and roll back if it regresses.
Maria: add a kv cache debug flag to log eviction counts for 5m window. helps confirm if eviction correlates with p95 spikes.
Raj: small caveat — token_aware increases scheduler CPU because it inspects sequence-lengths before enqueue. on low-ram nodes CPU becomes the bottleneck sometimes. we should cap concurrency if CPU climbs.
Anna: ok plan: Kevin will push per-pool override + kv debug. Maria will watch eviction logs. Raj will gate a token_aware experiment with concurrency cap. I'll monitor p95 and error budget.
Kevin: pushing override now to acme-internal (canary). payload: `{"batching":{"mode":"token_aware","max_batch_size":8,"token_budget_target":1024,"queue_timeout_ms":12},"kv":{"eviction_threshold_pct":65}}`
perf-bot: [info] canary deployed to acme-internal pool (id: pool-87) at 1859004440
Kevin: initial traces after override look promising — p95 down ~8% at first glance. will let it run 10m and then compare.
Maria: eviction logs: counts dropped from ~420 evictions/min to ~80 evictions/min after override (first 3 min).
Raj: CPU on scheduler ticked from 65% -> 78% (expected). I've set pool concurrency_limit: 10 for safety.
Anna: good. let's keep canary for 30m then decide rollforward. also file an action to revisit kernel-selector heuristics to avoid forcing fused-kernel on mismatch-prone traffic.
Kevin: filing perf ticket: PERF-8723 w/ snippets + traces. linking here once done.
Anna: thanks all. if anyone sees anomalies ping me @Anna. :thumbsup:
Kevin: PERF-8723: https://redwood/issue/PERF-8723 (added traces + canary config)
perf-bot: [resolved] alert acknowledged, monitoring continues.
